summary: Prolonged generation cutoff during batched long-context priming causing client timeouts
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 504/connection-timeout errors when requesting large max_output values and deep priming history in a single call. Impact: All generation requests that include an ~80k token context plus a 120k max_output budget are intermittently timing out after 90 seconds in the hosted Dedicated pool. Occurrence window: started 2026-03-11 09:15 UTC and recurred in bursts through 2026-03-12. Customer observed failures across multiple runs and client SDKs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer account API key in Dedicated pool (NimbleDocs dedicated namespace).
2) Send POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-open-v1-70b, temperature=0.2, max_output_tokens=120000, and include an application history ~80k tokens as the prompt.
3) Enable streaming in client and set client-side timeout to 90s.
4) Repeat 5-10 times in rapid succession (multi-tenant traffic present).
Expected: streaming begins and completes without server-side 504. Observed: request stalls, server-side finalizer times out and client receives 504 or connection reset.
observed_behavior: Requests with very large prompt + large max_output consistently hit server-side timeouts in bursts. Tail latency climbs from ~2s to >120s for finalization steps, and streaming stalls with no progress before final disconnect.
expected_behavior: Long-context requests should either be accepted and progress streamed until completion within SLOs, or fail fast with clear error (e.g., unsupported token budget) rather than silent stalls leading to 504s.

2026-03-11T09:23:44Z - http - responded 504 to client request id=xyz
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): validated customer reproduction, confirmed behavior isolated to dedicated pool in us-east-1 and to requests with combined very large context+max_output budgets.

SRE telemetry: observed sustained increase in finalizer queue length correlated with long-context requests. GPU kernel swap rate spiked during incident windows. Short low-latency requests continued to be served normally.

Hypothesis: recent scheduler change (dynamic batch coalescing v2) introduced heuristics that aggressively coalesced long-context requests into mixed batches with short requests. This caused long-running batches to occupy GPU for extended periods and produced priority inversion, causing finalizer/backpressure thrashing and KV cache evictions for queued long-context requests.

Further evidence: sampling of scheduler traces showed multiple mixed batches where a single long-context request queued with many short requests; mixed-batch kernel selection forced fallback code paths that perform additional KV materialization and repeated kernel swaps.
Related config change: rollout of dynamic batch coalescing v2 on 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC (PR r-infra#5483) — referenced in related_github_prs.
comments: 2026-03-11 - Asha (support): Opened ticket after customer shared logs and curl reproducer; initial workaround suggested lowering max_output to 10k.
2026-03-11 - Miguel (SRE): Confirmed reproduction in staging with dedicated-like load; creating scheduler experiment to isolate batch behavior.

2026-03-12 - SRE run: Rolled temporary rollback of dynamic coalescing heuristic in prod:us-east-1 for dedicated pool at 2026-03-12T04:30Z; observed finalizer queue length drop and no new 504s for same reproducer.
2026-03-12 - Customer (NimbleDocs): Verified with test harness; confirmed failures stopped after rollback. Customer requested follow-up and root cause analysis.

2026-03-13 - Miguel: Deployed targeted patch to scheduler to isolate long-context requests into long-request lanes and avoid mixed-batch kernel fallbacks; added telemetry to detect mixed-batch occurrences. Patch rolled out to us-east-1 dedicated pool at 2026-03-13T10:15Z.
resolution: Root cause: scheduler dynamic batch coalescing v2 caused mixed batches that triggered fallback kernel paths and repeated KV cache reloads, leading to finalizer queue bloating and timeouts for long-context requests. Fixes applied: 1) immediate rollback of the aggressive coalescing heuristic in prod:us-east-1 dedicated pools (mitigation), 2) targeted scheduler patch to create dedicated long-request lanes and avoid mixed-batch kernel selection, 3) added telemetry and an alert for mixed-batch rate and finalizer queue length. Follow-ups: extend mixed-batch tests in CI, update rollout checklist for scheduler heuristics, and notify customers with recommended best-practices (reduce max_output or use dedicated pinned instances for extreme budgets). Customer notified and confirmed recovery. Ticket closed after verification by customer and SRE.
